routine_modules.title: Module 0: Before You Begin
routine_modules.description: Guitar basics — how to hold and tune the instrument before you start playing.

routine_modules.title: Module 1: First Steps (A & D)
routine_modules.description: Your first two chords and your first chord change.

routine_modules.title: Module 2: 8 Essential Beginner Chord Grips
routine_modules.description: Lock in the eight open chords every beginner needs: A, D, E, Em, Am, Dm, D7, G.

routine_modules.title: Module 3: Capo, Minor Chords & Up Strums
routine_modules.description: Understand minor chords, get one-minute changes between them, and learn the capo.

routine_modules.title: Module 4: Metronome, Stretches & THE Strumming Pattern
routine_modules.description: Add Dm to your kit and start strumming along with a steady pulse.

routine_modules.title: Module 5: More Chords (C and G7)
routine_modules.description: C is the trickiest open chord; G7 is your gateway to country and blues.

routine_modules.title: Module 6: Time Signatures & 6/8 Strumming
routine_modules.description: Step outside 4/4: feel a waltz in 3/4 and a slow ballad in 6/8.

routine_modules.title: Module 7: Strumming Mechanics, Dynamics, Up Strums
routine_modules.description: Stop being a robot - add accents, ghost strums, and groove.

routine_modules.title: Module 8: How to PASS Grade 1
routine_modules.description: Three song-form tests. If you can play these cleanly in time, you've passed Grade 1.

routine_modules.title: Module 9: The F Chord
routine_modules.description: The dreaded F. Tackle the full barre or one of the easier 3-string voicings.

routine_modules.title: Module 10: Fingerpicking Basics
routine_modules.description: Put the pick down. Thumb plays bass, fingers play melody.

routine_modules.title: Module 11: Major Scale & Improvisation
routine_modules.description: Your first scale, your first solo.

routine_modules.title: Module 12: Power Chords & Palm Muting
routine_modules.description: Two-finger chords that work everywhere. Add palm muting and you have rock.

routine_modules.title: Module 13: 7th Chord Grips & Blues
routine_modules.description: Dominant 7ths - the sound of the blues.

routine_modules.title: Module 14: Slash Chords
routine_modules.description: Chord/bass. C/G means a C chord with G in the bass.

routine_modules.title: Module 15: How to PASS Grade 2
routine_modules.description: Three big tests. Cleanly played, in time, no stops.

routine_exercises.title: Tuning your guitar
routine_exercises.instructions: Use a clip-on tuner or phone app. Tune low to high: E A D G B E.

routine_exercises.title: Holding the guitar
routine_exercises.instructions: Sit with the guitar on your right leg, neck slightly raised.

routine_exercises.title: Holding the pick
routine_exercises.instructions: Grip lightly between thumb and curled index finger.

routine_exercises.title: Reading chord boxes
routine_exercises.instructions: 6 vertical lines = strings (low E left). Horizontal lines = frets.

routine_exercises.title: Reading TAB
routine_exercises.instructions: 6 horizontal lines = strings (high E top). Numbers = fret to press.

routine_exercises.title: Practice the A chord
routine_exercises.instructions: Three fingers in the 2nd fret. Press near the fret wire. Strum 5 strings (mute low E).

routine_exercises.title: Practice the D chord
routine_exercises.instructions: Triangle shape on strings 1-3. Strum 4 strings.

routine_exercises.title: One-minute change: A <-> D
routine_exercises.instructions: Count how many clean changes you make in 60 seconds. Beat your score each session.

routine_exercises.title: First song in A and D
routine_exercises.instructions: Three Little Birds uses A, D, and E. Start by playing A and D only.

routine_exercises.title: Practice A
routine_exercises.instructions: Three fingers cramped in fret 2. Curl them so you don't mute strings.

routine_exercises.title: Practice D
routine_exercises.instructions: Push fingers right up against the frets for a clean tone.

routine_exercises.title: Practice E
routine_exercises.instructions: All three fingers in fret 1 and 2. Strum all six strings.

routine_exercises.title: Practice Em
routine_exercises.instructions: Easiest open chord: two fingers in fret 2 on strings A and D.

routine_exercises.title: Practice Am
routine_exercises.instructions: Same shape as E, shifted one string up.

routine_exercises.title: Practice Dm
routine_exercises.instructions: Mute low E and A. Three fingers form a triangle on strings 1-3.

routine_exercises.title: Practice D7
routine_exercises.instructions: Like D, but the index moves to the high E string.

routine_exercises.title: Practice G
routine_exercises.instructions: The big stretch chord. Use fingers 2-3-4 to keep finger 1 free.

routine_exercises.title: Practice Em
routine_exercises.instructions: Two fingers, sounds sad. Strum all six strings.

routine_exercises.title: Practice Am
routine_exercises.instructions: Three fingers, classic 'sad chord' grip.

routine_exercises.title: One-minute change: Em <-> Am
routine_exercises.instructions: Pivot on the index finger - it doesn't move between the two chords.

routine_exercises.title: What are minor chords?
routine_exercises.instructions: Minor = sad/sombre. Major = bright/happy. The difference is one note (the third).

routine_exercises.title: Using a capo
routine_exercises.instructions: A capo raises the pitch of every string. Same shapes, different key.

routine_exercises.title: Practice Dm
routine_exercises.instructions: Same triangle as D, but the high E is fretted at 1 with the index.

routine_exercises.title: One-minute change: Am <-> Dm
routine_exercises.instructions: Both use fingers 1, 2, 3. Try to lift and place all three together.

routine_exercises.title: Stretches for guitarists
routine_exercises.instructions: Wrist rolls, finger fans, and forearm stretches before and after practice.

routine_exercises.title: Strum 'Old Faithful' over Let It Be
routine_exercises.instructions: D - DU - UDU per bar. Keep your hand moving even when you don't strum.

routine_exercises.title: Practice C
routine_exercises.instructions: Three fingers spread across three frets. Curl your fingers to avoid muting.

routine_exercises.title: Practice G7
routine_exercises.instructions: Like G with the high E played at fret 1 instead of fret 3.

routine_exercises.title: One-minute change: C <-> G
routine_exercises.instructions: Anchor the ring finger on the A string fret 3 (it stays put for both shapes).

routine_exercises.title: One-minute change: C <-> Am
routine_exercises.instructions: Top two fingers don't move - just lift the third finger off.

routine_exercises.title: Knockin' in 3/4
routine_exercises.instructions: Same chords, three beats per bar. Counts 'one-two-three'.

routine_exercises.title: Knockin' in 6/8
routine_exercises.instructions: Six pulses per bar grouped in two. Counts 'ONE-two-three-FOUR-five-six'.

routine_exercises.title: What is a time signature?
routine_exercises.instructions: Top number = beats per bar. Bottom number = which note value gets one beat.

routine_exercises.title: Strum I-V-vi-IV in C
routine_exercises.instructions: Keep your strumming hand moving constantly. Loud on beat 1, soft on the rest.

routine_exercises.title: Strum the 50s progression
routine_exercises.instructions: Try a slow eighth-note strum and emphasize beats 2 and 4 like a snare.

routine_exercises.title: Strumming mechanics
routine_exercises.instructions: Strum from the wrist, not the elbow. Loose grip on the pick.

routine_exercises.title: Dynamics and accents
routine_exercises.instructions: Hit some strums harder than others - that's where the groove lives.

routine_exercises.title: Play Three Little Birds
routine_exercises.instructions: Smooth A-D-A-E loop with no pauses.

routine_exercises.title: Play Knockin' on Heaven's Door
routine_exercises.instructions: Two bars per chord. Hold each chord steady - no rushing the change.

routine_exercises.title: Play Zombie
routine_exercises.instructions: Em-C-G-D loop. The classic 90s alt-rock progression.

routine_exercises.title: Practice F
routine_exercises.instructions: Index finger barres strings 1 and 2 at fret 1. Keep the thumb behind the neck.

routine_exercises.title: One-minute change: C <-> F
routine_exercises.instructions: The hardest beginner change. Move three fingers together as one shape.

routine_exercises.title: Play Let It Be
routine_exercises.instructions: C - G - Am - F. Now you can play it properly with the F.

routine_exercises.title: Travis picking primer
routine_exercises.instructions: Thumb alternates between two bass strings. Fingers fill in on top.

routine_exercises.title: Fingerpick Em7
routine_exercises.instructions: Easiest chord to start with - only two fingers on the fretboard.

routine_exercises.title: Fingerpick the Wonderwall verse
routine_exercises.instructions: Pick instead of strum. Same chords, totally different mood.

routine_exercises.title: G major scale, shape 1
routine_exercises.instructions: Two octaves starting on the low E string. Memorize the pattern.

routine_exercises.title: Finding root notes
routine_exercises.instructions: Every chord has a root. Find the root of each chord on the low E string.

routine_exercises.title: Improvise over I-IV-V in G
routine_exercises.instructions: Use the G major scale. Aim for the root note when each chord changes.

routine_exercises.title: Power chord shapes
routine_exercises.instructions: Root + 5th. Two notes, movable, sounds great with distortion.

routine_exercises.title: Strum 12-bar blues in E
routine_exercises.instructions: Use E5, A5, B5 power chords. Strict downstrokes for the rock feel.

routine_exercises.title: Palm-muting technique
routine_exercises.instructions: Rest the side of your strumming-hand palm on the strings near the bridge.

routine_exercises.title: Practice A7
routine_exercises.instructions: Like A, but lift the ring finger off.

routine_exercises.title: Practice D7
routine_exercises.instructions: Triangular shape, but the high E moves to fret 2.

routine_exercises.title: Practice E7
routine_exercises.instructions: Like E, but lift the ring finger off.

routine_exercises.title: Play 12-bar blues in A
routine_exercises.instructions: The classic 12-bar form. A7 - D7 - E7. The shuffle.

routine_exercises.title: Play 12-bar blues in E
routine_exercises.instructions: Same form, different key. Use E7, A7, B7.

routine_exercises.title: What are slash chords?
routine_exercises.instructions: The letter after the slash is the bass note. Used for smooth bass lines.

routine_exercises.title: D/F# concept
routine_exercises.instructions: D chord with F# (low E string, fret 2) in the bass. Wrap your thumb over.

routine_exercises.title: Strum Sweet Home Alabama
routine_exercises.instructions: D - Cadd9 - G is the signature riff. Sounds great with picking too.

routine_exercises.title: Play With or Without You
routine_exercises.instructions: Four-chord loop, simple but exposing - any timing wobble is obvious.

routine_exercises.title: Play Let It Be
routine_exercises.instructions: Including the F. No skipping or substituting easier chords.

routine_exercises.title: 12-bar blues at speed
routine_exercises.instructions: Blues in A at 110 bpm. The shuffle should feel locked in.
